key_insight: Neural surrogates trained on quantum-hardware QAOA samples accelerated autocorrelation decay in constrained Boltzmann sampling with over 1,000 binary variables.
engineering_relevance: A divide-and-conquer implementation enables quantum-assisted proposals for large constrained sampling problems without placing the full system on quantum hardware.
method: Generate QAOA training samples using an IBM Quantum Heron r2 processor.
Train neural surrogates to support quantum-enhanced MCMC proposals.
Use a divide-and-conquer strategy to handle larger systems through subproblems.
evidence_signal: Experiments covered N=144 and N=1064; at N=1064, autocorrelation decay per MCMC step was approximately 5.2× and 12.3× faster than global and local Kawasaki dynamics, respectively.
watch_item: Larger subproblem blocks challenged neural-surrogate learning, and faster decay per MCMC step does not establish end-to-end runtime advantage.
paper_title: Hardware Demonstration of Neural-Surrogated Quantum-Enhanced MCMC for Large-Scale Constrained Boltzmann Sampling
